PHF1 fusions are gene rearrangements that occur in certain tumors; most notably ossifying fibromyxoid tumors (OFMT); and are also found in some other cancers like endometrial stromal sarcoma. These fusions involve the PHF1 gene; which is involved in gene transcription regulation; and are linked to the development and progression of these tumors by altering gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Common fusion partners include EP400 and MEAF6. The EP400-PHF1 Fusion leads to truncation of the EP400 tumor suppressor gene and is considered likely oncogenic.
